findings.title: Bound connect-burst batches by bytes, not only by event count
findings.comment: The defect is real, and the code is in this range: socket-port.ts and the E10 burst in session-stream.ts are both new here. `republish` (session-stream.ts:219-223) cuts the ring (RING_SIZE 5,000) into slices of BATCH_MAX=500 events only. `SocketPort.postMessage` (src/shared/host/socket-port.ts) writes each line without checking its size. It returns true unless writableLength passes WRITABLE_CAP, and the cursor moves past every batch for which it returned true. On main's side, `SocketPort`'s `splitLines` (LINE_CAP 64 MiB) calls `fail()` and destroys the connection when a line is over the cap. `tool.result` and `user.message` keep content blocks loosely (`ContentBlockSchema = z.looseObject`). The pass3 fixtures (p1-maws-browser.jsonl) show the base64 image `source.data` carried inline, and BROWSER_SCREENSHOT_MAX_BYTES is 3.5 MiB, about 4.9 MB of base64. Failure: a kept session takes a dozen or more fullPage screenshots while the app is away. At reconnect the 500-event batch is over 64 MiB, so main drops the connection, but the host has already moved `deliveredTo` past that batch, and the events never reach the client on the next burst. The 256 MiB `WRITABLE_CAP` path has the same problem: the burst is one synchronous loop, so if the whole tail passes 256 MiB, `fail()` destroys the socket with earlier batches still in its write buffer, and those batches were already counted delivered. This contradicts the exactly-once intent stated in the header comment. I rate it P3, not P2: it needs tens of MiB of inline images within 500 consecutive events, which typical viewport screenshots of a few hundred KB do not reach. The live path (`emitBatch` with its 16 ms window) is not affected in practice.

findings.title: Skip the screenshot record when the call was withdrawn while it was being read
findings.comment: Verified in src/engine-host/tool-server/browser.ts. After `bridge.request` returns 'answered', `screenshotAnswer` never checks `ctx.signal`. It awaits `stat`, `readFile`, then `deliverables.exclusive(...write(record))`, and that write can queue behind other writers for the same session. server.ts (line ~182) drops the response with `if (controller.signal.aborted || call.answered) return;` when a `control_cancel_request` or `notifications/cancelled` arrives in that window (it aborts with 'withdrawn' at line ~136), or when the process exits. Result: the screenshot deliverable record is written and announced with a toolUseId whose result the model never received. That breaks the function's own documented invariant, "A record is written only for a picture the model receives." The window is a few milliseconds and the leftover is one extra deliverable that does no harm, so this is P3.

findings.title: Take the reload expectation's scope from the CLI result, not a 'user' default
findings.comment: Verified. runner.ts passes `scope: i.scope ?? 'user'` to `reloadAfter`, and reload-after.ts's `ReloadChange.scope` comment says "the CLI's default, user, when the input named none". `commandLine` (src/shared/plugins/cli.ts:39) passes no `--scope` when the input has none. I ran the installed CLI's help: `plugin enable` and `plugin disable` say `(default: auto-detect)`, and only `uninstall` says `(default: "user")`. Failure: an enable or disable sent through the plugins IPC without a scope, for a plugin installed at project or local scope. The CLI changes that scope, but `applies()` treats it as user scope. Sessions in other directories then get the expectation, a second reload after another SETTLE_MS, and are reported `not_reflected`. The defect is latent: the only renderer callers always pass a scope (Installed.tsx `scopeOfRow`, Available.tsx `'user'`). The IPC input schema still makes scope optional, so P3.

Interrupt and cancel paths (notifications/cancelled, control_cancel_request, exit with pending asks, panes or browser requests) leaving no pending state.
